reason: Measured baseline progress and remaining source length project the full legacy regression beyond the first evaluation worker's one-hour deadline. Separate concept evaluation from PII retention instead of dropping cases or changing decoding.
concept_worker: The RTX 4090 retains its completed/in-progress dev and concept-test baselines. It runs the selected candidate on those same 100 and 159 cases, respectively. Its partial legacy baseline is excluded.
legacy_worker: A separate RTX 3090 runs both original-model and selected-candidate evaluations on the same 300 original PII documents. Within each paired comparison, hardware, runtime, weights, source data, evaluator and decoding settings are matched. The two evaluation suites use different GPU types; no latency claim or cross-hardware accuracy delta is substituted for a within-suite comparison.
unchanged: Training, data, gold labels, checkpoint selection, model configuration, generation settings and numeric screening thresholds remain unchanged. This is an execution scheduling change.
spend: The four-hour RTX 4090 training cap at USD 0.89/hour, one-hour RTX 4090 concept-worker cap at USD 0.89/hour, and two-hour RTX 3090 regression-worker cap at USD 0.22/hour total at most USD 4.89 of quoted GPU runtime. Collect verified artifacts and terminate earlier when complete.
capacity: The USD 0.50/hour offering failed during provisioning with no running instance. The replacement uses a USD 0.22/hour GPU.ai community RTX 3090 offering with a two-hour cap. Transferred data consists of public-source synthetic evaluation/replay, newly authored fictional scenarios, source code and the selected adapter; the unpublished fourth training corpus is not transferred.
